page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, providing 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via two threads per core. Architecture includes x86_64 instructions with AVX-512 vector support, SHA extensions, and AES cryptography acceleration. The system delivers 1024.0 GB of memory, yielding a high ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources also include 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, with no discrete GPUs attached.

Performance testing reflects strong compute and data manipulation metrics. Single-core execution achieves top-tier results, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2884.0, a stress-ng single-core rating in the top 10%, and gzip compression throughput of 41.3 GB/sec. Multi-threaded processing reaches a Geekbench multi-core score of 22126.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 58692.46. Memory benchmarks record large-block uncached read speeds of 101.48 GB/sec and write speeds of 67.44 GB/sec, while in-memory operations register 52.64 million Redis SET operations per second.

Given the high memory footprint paired with a modest vCPU count, the instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for applications bottlenecked by memory capacity rather than compute parallelism. The bundled 7560 GB NVMe storage provides rapid local scratch space for temporary workloads. Tradeoffs include average multi-core CPU scaling and lower throughput for compute-bound tasks like large parameter LLM generation, where 70B model text generation yields only 2.44 tokens per second. The server is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, and high-memory analytics processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a 32-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz across 16 physical cores. Configured with 1024.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a high 32:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance, recording 2884.0 in Geekbench single-core and top-decile compression speeds, coupled with strong PassMark CPU and memory metrics. While multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth fall into competitive mid-to-high ranges, LLM generation on large models suffers from the absence of dedicated accelerators. The server is well suited for memory-bound workloads, including massive in-memory databases, real-time data caching, and large-scale data transformation pipelines that require significant RAM and fast local scratch storage.
